newsitem.title: INDIA: SQUASH-ANGRY GREGORY THROUGH TO LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-ANGRY GREGORY THROUGH TO LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Paul Gregory accused the referee of "costing me my wages" and still recovered from the brink of defeat to upset the seedings on Tuesday and earn himself one of his biggest pay days in the $105,000 Mahindra international, the world's second-richest squash tournament.

Gregory's 8-15 15-8 12-15 15-13 15-8 win over last year's World Open finalist Del Harris in a battle of former British national champions earned him an unexpected quarter-final with top-seeded Australian Rodney Eyles.

Gregory, who has dual nationality and plays for Greece, had to come back from 8-11 down in the fourth game and from within three points of defeat at 11-12 against an opponent who tired within sight of victory. Gregory also had to conquer himself.

He was beside himself with fury at having a good shot called down near the end of the third game and once left the court to argue with the officials. Gregory and Harris both threw their rackets in fits of temper but neither was warned.

Eyles achieved revenge against the brilliant Canadian Jonathan Power. The world number 11 had beaten the Australian en route to winning the Tournament of Champions in New York in October but now found Eyles in a determined and consistent frame of mind and was beaten 15-13 15-12 15-5.

Power also had a novel line in taunting a referee whose decisions annoyed him. He requested a let in the third game when the match was almost lost, got it and then refused it, saying with a grin: "I was just testing you."
Another quarter-finalist, Mark Cairns, may be about to snatch the last place in the eight-man Super Series final from Australian Anthony Hill.

Hill walked out of his first-round match on Monday, leaving Cairns and another Englishman, Simon Parke, with a chance of making up the points difference between them and the Australian in the Super Series table.
Cairns scored a 15-13 15-12 15-11 win over the improving Egyptian Omar El Borolossy and earned a meeting with another unseeded quarter-finalist, Irishman Derek Ryan.
